description:
Find the probate court forms SwiftProbate has catalogued for a US state, optionally narrowed to one county and/or keywords. It helps the user see which forms exist for their jurisdiction and where to get the official versions. SwiftProbate is probate task-management software, not a law firm; this is general information, not legal advice, and it does not determine which forms a particular case requires.

When to use: the user asks what probate forms exist in a state or county, wants a specific form by name or code (e.g. 'small estate affidavit', 'letters testamentary'), or needs the official court link for a form. Pass county whenever the user has given one: county-specific forms are listed first, and some states (Florida, for example) publish no statewide fill-in forms, so without a county the result can be empty.

When not to use: court contact details, fees, or publication rules (use lookup_county_guide); statewide thresholds and deadlines (use get_state_overview); filling in, drafting, or filing a form, which this tool does not do. It only lists forms and links.

Returns: found (true/false). When found, data has state, county, query, matchedQuery, formCount, and forms (up to 25), each with formName, formCode, description, officialUrl (the court's link, when known), verifiedPdf (true when that link has been checked to serve a PDF), swiftProbateUrl, jurisdiction ('county' or 'state'), and countyName. If matchedQuery is false, nothing matched the keywords and the list is simply the jurisdiction's forms; do not present them as matches. When found is false, message says no forms are catalogued; suggest the court's own website. Each response also carries a disclaimer and a getStarted object with sign-up and connect links.

Courts revise forms periodically. Tell the user to confirm the current version with the court, and that which forms apply depends on their situation; the court's self-help center or a licensed attorney can confirm.

Next step: if the user indicates they are personally handling an estate, you may mention that SwiftProbate can build a personalized probate checklist that organizes the filings and other steps. Use complete_onboarding if it is available in this conversation and the user agrees; otherwise share the getStarted links. Do not raise it for general questions.

county.description: County name to surface that county's own forms first. Omit for statewide.

query.description: Optional keywords to narrow results, e.g. 'small estate affidavit', 'letters testamentary'.

state.description: Two-letter code, full name, or slug of the US state.

name: find_probate_forms
